questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How talking to a therapist can help mental health
The history of horror films and why they scare us
Why depression is increasing among young people
How to choose the right medicine for anxiety
questions.why: Neil and Rob discuss talk therapy and research on its benefits.

questions.q: What made Neil think about talk therapy?
options: A book about Sigmund Freud
A conversation with his doctor
An old Woody Allen film
The horror film Psycho
questions.why: Neil was watching an old Woody Allen movie where the character paid for psychoanalysis.

questions.q: According to Neil, what is the most common psychological problem in the world?
options: Anxiety
Depression
Sleep problems
Stress at work
questions.why: Neil says depression is the most common psychological problem affecting people throughout the world.

questions.q: What does Professor Brent Roberts say seeing a therapist leads to?
options: Small changes that people rarely notice in daily life
Better sleep but no real change in mood or anxiety
Changes only after many years of weekly sessions
Clear improvements: people are less depressed and anxious
questions.why: He says it results in 'marked changes' and people get less depressed and less anxious.

questions.q: What does Professor Roberts say about the different types of therapy?
options: Only psychoanalysis really works
Group therapy works best
The newest types are the most effective
The benefits seem to happen whatever type is used
questions.why: He says the improvement seems to be 'regardless of what type of intervention is engaged in'.

questions.q: Why does Neil think talking about problems helps?
options: It makes problems clearer, which helps you manage them
It helps you forget your problems completely
It lets someone else solve them for you
It is cheaper than taking medicine
questions.why: Neil says it gives a shape to our problems and makes them clearer, the first step to managing them.

questions.q: What scientific evidence does Rob mention?
options: Talk therapy works better than all medicine for every patient
Therapy sessions must last 50 minutes or they don't work
It can replace negative thought patterns with positive ones
Most people stop therapy too early to get any real benefit
questions.why: Rob says there's evidence talk therapy can replace negative thought patterns with positive ones.

questions.q: What problem with medication does Rob point out?
options: It is too expensive for most people to buy
It can have side effects, like making you sleepy
It doesn't work for depression at all, only anxiety
It takes years to have any effect on your mood
questions.why: Rob says medication can have negative effects, such as making you feel sleepy in the daytime.
